title: Your containment GameDay
scenario: Your team wants evidence that one faulty lamp dependency cannot unnecessarily hide the chair and desk. Design one repeatable local experiment that demonstrates impact beyond the lamp, then test whether your mitigation contains it.
why: A fallback is justified by useful behavior preserved under a specific fault, not by an enabled checkbox. Your recommendation needs before-and-after evidence for the catalog or healthy products and an explicit statement of lost certainty.
reproduce: Choose Inventory or Shipping on the lamp branch and one fault: a measured delay or disconnection. Choose availability or delivery catalog. A +1500 ms delay can pressure shared workers; disconnection demonstrates aggregate error propagation.
ready: {{ready}} Use only the two exposed lamp fault controls; the other product paths are the healthy comparison group.
assignment: Can you reproduce a wider customer impact and then contain it to the affected product’s missing information?

tasks.title: Define a propagation hypothesis
tasks.instruction: Name the catalog view, lamp dependency, exact fault/magnitude, healthy comparison products, propagation mechanism and abort condition. Choose customer results and worker/product metrics that could disprove your hypothesis.

tasks.title: Record a healthy comparison window
tasks.instruction: Measure all three products, catalog latency/status, worker queue and changes in cumulative rejections over a fixed window. Keep supplied traffic unchanged for every phase.

tasks.title: Reproduce impact beyond the lamp
tasks.instruction: Apply only your chosen fault. Measure the same view and healthy products. Record whether impact spreads by queuing, rejection, aggregate failure or a combination. If no wider effect appears, report that honestly and revise the experiment before recommending mitigation.

tasks.title: Choose a mechanism-specific mitigation
tasks.instruction: Remove the fault before configuring. Use a short dependency timeout for a slow call, enable fallback/breaker for the relevant dependency, and justify the missing-data behavior. Do not claim fallback alone releases workers.

tasks.title: Repeat exactly and recommend
tasks.instruction: Reapply the identical fault at the same magnitude and traffic. Show whether chair/desk remain useful, whether catalog status/time improves, and what lamp information remains unavailable. Include probe behavior and exact rollback instructions. {{cleanup}}

done: A teammate can reproduce the fault, traffic, three-phase measurements, mitigation and rollback.
You demonstrated and measured a wider impact before mitigation, then compared healthy products and catalog usefulness under the identical fault.
You distinguished timeout, breaker and fallback, described remaining uncertainty/probe spikes, and restored all three products.
solution: There is no single correct experiment. It needs healthy, faulted and mitigated phases, the exact same fault/traffic, a wider customer impact and an honest remaining trade-off.

Example: +1500 ms on lamp Shipping during delivery catalog refresh. Default waiting can consume shared workers and delay the aggregate. Set a 400 ms Shipping timeout with fallback/breaker, then repeat the exact delay.

Chair and desk should retain live stock/quotes while the lamp quote becomes unavailable. The breaker probes every 5 seconds and may cause short spikes. Compare queue pressure and rejection-rate changes, not lifetime totals.
If your chosen fault causes only aggregate failure and no capacity pressure, state that distinction. Finish with verified live results for all three products.

fields.label: Experiment plan
fields.prompt: State route, dependency, fault, magnitude, expected blast radius, and abort condition.

fields.label: Steady state and hypothesis
fields.prompt: What did you measure before the fault, and what do you predict? {{measurementGuidance}}

fields.label: Fault result
fields.prompt: Record your actual fault commands, time window, customer effect, and dependency signals. {{measurementGuidance}}

fields.label: {{mitigationLabel}}
fields.prompt: Which timeout/fallback settings did you change, and why? {{mitigationGuidance}}

fields.label: Identical-fault validation
fields.prompt: Reapply the same fault and compare route latency, success, and fallback behavior. {{measurementGuidance}}

fields.label: Conclusion, trade-off, and rollback
fields.prompt: Did resilience improve? What risk remains? How did you restore the clean state?

overview.title: 4 · Prove useful containment
overview.description: Design an experiment whose mitigation visibly protects the catalog or healthy products, and document its trade-off.
